title: Rule out k-cycles in Collatz via case-analysis extension

problemStatement.plain: Formal investigation in number theory: Rule out k-cycles in Collatz via case-analysis extension.

currentState.focus: Completed: j=1 uniqueness, extended halving bounds j=5..8, Eliahou axiom.

knowledge.progressSummary: Formalized j=1 cycle uniqueness (3n+1=2^M·n → n=1,M=2), extended halving bounds to j=5..8, proved minimum cycle lengths, axiomatized Eliahou 1993 bound. 0 sorries, 1 axiom.
builtItems: min_halvings_five_odd through min_halvings_eight_odd — halving bounds for j=5..8
min_cycle_length_j5 through min_cycle_length_j8 — cycle length bounds
eliahou_cycle_bound axiom — non-trivial cycles have period > 17 billion
oq01_case_analysis_limited — all cycles with period ≤ 17 billion reduce to {1,4,2}
insights: 3n+1 = 2^M*n rearranges to n*(2^M-3)=1, forcing n|1 so n=1 (and M=2)
For period-4 cycles: j=1 gives 5n=1 (impossible), j≥2 violates 2^(4-j)>3^j
Halving bounds grow as ceil(j*log2(3))≈1.585j; min cycle lengths ≈ 2.585j
Parity case explosion: 2^k patterns for k-cycle makes direct analysis infeasible for large k
Eliahou (1993) uses algebraic sum bounds to prove 17-billion lower bound in one argument
